title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
evidence_locator: Sec. 3, Algorithm 1, lines 94-140 of arXiv HTML
supports: The proposer inspects prior code, scores, and traces, then generates executable harness candidates that are evaluated as whole programs.
boundary: Rich history access and candidate-level code search do not independently test an uncompiled behavioral hypothesis.

title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
evidence_locator: Secs. 3.2-3.4, especially HTML lines 200-207
supports: Failure patterns must be recurrent and addressable; each proposal is a minimal executable branch and is then regression-tested.
boundary: Addressability filtering precedes proposal, but the first behavioral test object is already a candidate harness edit.

title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.1 and Fig. 2; HTML lines 102-118 and 137-153
supports: A trained engineer converts failure batches into validated executable patches and receives same-batch outcome reward after rerunning the frozen target.
boundary: Mechanism validity, target execution, and patch realization remain jointly reflected in patch-level reward.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
evidence_locator: Secs. 3.2-3.3 and Algorithm 1; HTML lines 137-182
supports: Layered trajectory evidence and edit manifests attach root cause, predicted fixes, and regression risks to each file-level change.
boundary: The prediction is verified by the next candidate-level rollout; the paper reports regression blindness and non-additive component interactions.

title: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
evidence_locator: Abstract and introduction; arXiv abstract lines 16-19
supports: Sparse, high-variance long-horizon outcomes make failure attribution and candidate selection unreliable; demonstrations improve diagnosis and editing.
boundary: It improves proposer evidence but still evaluates materialized harness edits.

title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
evidence_locator: Sec. 4.3, especially HTML lines 123-148
supports: Weak agents may fail to activate a relevant harness artifact or may load it but fail to follow it faithfully; harness benefit is model-dependent.
boundary: This is a measurement and diagnosis study, not a pre-compilation realizability gate in an optimizer.

title: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
evidence_locator: Secs. 4.1 and 4.4; HTML lines 73-112
supports: A population of executable harness candidates is proposed and committed from unlabeled execution proxies during evaluation.
boundary: The method exposes proxy and judge reliability as bottlenecks but does not insert a mechanism experiment before candidate generation.

title: Shepherd: Enabling Programmable Meta-Agents via Reversible Agentic Execution Traces
evidence_locator: Introduction and Sec. 5.2; HTML lines 28-34
supports: Typed, reversible traces enable exact fork/replay and counterfactual replay optimization that validates proposed fixes from the first behavior-divergence point.
boundary: Fork/replay is not novel; the closest overlap is validation by branching, so novelty must rest on hypothesis-first pre-compilation gating and realizability.

title: TraceGraph: Shared Decision Landscapes for Diagnosing and Improving Agent Trajectories
evidence_locator: Abstract and trap-aware recovery pipeline; arXiv lines 3-5
supports: Continuation policies are compared from the same failure-prone prefix, with provider-specific effects.
boundary: The objective is diagnosis and runtime recovery rather than deciding whether an uncompiled harness hypothesis deserves persistence.

title: Harnessing LLM Agents with Skill Programs
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.1, HTML lines 134-145; Sec. 3.3, lines 157-161
supports: Program Functions explicitly encode should_activate and intervene, and candidate PFs pass executable validation plus teacher review before admission.
boundary: Guard plus intervention and executable skill-library validation are prior art; HASP does not separately test whether the fixed Student can perform a hook_model semantic responsibility before compilation.

title: HarnessBank: Semantic Gene-Bank Search with Gated Verification for Agent-Harness Self-Evolution
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.3, HTML lines 157-185
supports: Candidate harnesses pass validity, activation, paired-significance, and gain gates on a subset before full evaluation.
boundary: This strongly narrows novelty: gated screening and paired statistics exist, but its screening object is already an executable candidate harness.

title: DREvo: Distilling Recalibrated Historical Experience for Harness Self-Evolution
evidence_locator: Introduction and Secs. Function-Level Evidence Anchoring / State-Dependent Evidence Recalibration; HTML lines 21-29 and 63-78
supports: Historical evidence is anchored to functions, recalibrated for current harness state, and distilled into explicit search intent.
boundary: Evidence organization and rerouting are not enough for novelty; DREvo still emits and evaluates candidate harnesses.

title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
evidence_locator: Secs. 1 and 3.1; HTML lines 17-24 and 70-84
supports: Harness evolution is bounded by feedback fidelity and frozen-backbone capability; HSI keeps explicit editable boundaries and frozen anchors.
boundary: A backbone capability bound is stated, but no per-mechanism Student feasibility test is performed before implementation.

title: VeRO: A Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
evidence_locator: Sec. 1 and system overview; HTML lines 4-25
supports: Versioned snapshots, budget-enforced evaluation, and structured execution traces are enabling evaluation infrastructure.
boundary: These system properties should be framed as infrastructure, not the principal algorithmic novelty.

title: HarnessCompass: Guiding Automatic Harness Evolution toward Generalizable and Effective Agent Harnesses
evidence_locator: Introduction and main results; HTML lines 4-6 and 159-196
supports: Constrained evolution, proactive feedback, and component-wise optimization improve generalization and reduce cross-component interference.
boundary: Component decoupling is prior art; it does not compare multiple realizations of one implementation-independent mechanism under a Student-feasibility contract.

title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
evidence_locator: Secs. 3-4, especially HTML lines 35-82 and 104-133
supports: Harness evolution must be compared against budget-matched parallel sampling and sequential refinement and measured on held-out tasks.
boundary: Any claimed cost or utility benefit for Evidence-Gated evolution must survive these controls; current project runs do not yet do so.

title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
evidence_locator: Abstract and Secs. 3-4; arXiv HTML abstract lines 16-20
supports: Cross-trial memory can be hierarchical, agent-specific, and grounded in condensed collaboration trajectories and generalizable insights.
boundary: Agent-specific cross-trial memory is prior art; the open distinction is verification-stage provenance and optimizer-role consumption rather than runtime task-solving memory.

title: Intrinsic Memory Agents: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent LLM Systems through Structured Contextual Memory
evidence_locator: Abstract and Secs. 3.1-3.2; arXiv HTML abstract lines 16-19
supports: Role-aligned, agent-specific memories can evolve with agent outputs and preserve specialized perspectives.
boundary: Routing each memory to its corresponding role is not independently novel; this work does not derive optimizer lessons from typed gate rejections.

title: Scaling Teams or Scaling Time? Memory Enabled Lifelong Learning in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
evidence_locator: Secs. 3.2-3.4 and 4.5; arXiv HTML abstract lines 16-18
supports: Flexible memory topology controls who reads and writes episodic, procedural, and transactive memory; local role-specific topology can avoid cross-role interference.
boundary: The proposed three experience categories closely resemble episodic, procedural, and transactive memory, so category taxonomy is not a novelty claim.

title: When Search Becomes Memory: Turning Robot Design Trials into Transferable Skills
evidence_locator: Abstract and method Add/Diagnose/Merge; arXiv HTML abstract lines 16-18
supports: Search traces can be converted into an inspectable skill library with evidence-grounded positive/negative rules and evaluated designs while retaining an exploration path.
boundary: An experiment-direction map and evidence-linked search memory already have a close precedent outside harness evolution; the distinctive claim must concern typed gate provenance, scope, and false-pruning control.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
evidence_locator: Abstract and experience gathering/insight extraction method; arXiv abstract lines 16-20
supports: Agents can collect experiences, extract natural-language knowledge, and retrieve insights and past experiences without parameter updates.
boundary: Generic experiential learning is prior art; it does not specify role-scoped optimizer memories written from separate hypothesis, evidence, feasibility, and implementation verdicts.

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
evidence_locator: Abstract and method; arXiv HTML lines 16-20
supports: Structured memories can be dynamically linked and updated as new evidence arrives.
boundary: Dynamic memory organization is prior art and does not by itself establish safe search pruning or verification-grounded scope invalidation.
